A mask is a black-and-white video that follows your footage: **white character, black background**. Match its timing and framing to the source. For example, use the result of **Make a Subject Mask** in the **LTX 2.5 Edit & VFX** workflow.

1. **Add your mask.** Import it through **Assets**, then drag it onto a **Video** lane. Right-click its clip and choose **[Convert to Driver](https://github.com/SonderSaid/ComfyUI-Sonder-Editor/blob/main/docs/editor-basics.md#driver-clips)**. Keep your original footage on Video.
2. **Choose that Driver.** In **Controls → Generation → Mask video lane**, select the lane containing your mask.
3. **Choose the area to refine.** Under **Modes → Refine Pass Spatial Mask**, select **Refine Character** or **Refine Environment**.

The mask focuses refinement; it does not guarantee that everything outside the chosen area stays unchanged.

**Check the processed mask.** The preview turns on automatically with **Refine Character** or **Refine Environment**, and off with **Mask Off**. At the top of a viewport pane, open its source menu and choose **Mask Preview**. Click that pane’s **Run** to check the mask without running diffusion.

- **Use the finished video.** Saved videos include the timeline’s sound for the processed section. Your existing Audio lanes stay unchanged; no duplicate Audio lanes are added.
- **Change where results go.** The **Passes** choices set the save destinations automatically. After choosing a Mode, open **Controls → Editor** and use **Refine save as** and **Upscale save as**: **Take** adds the result to the timeline; **Video** saves it in Assets without placing it.
- **Choose the file quality.** In **Controls → Editor**, set **Refine output format** or **Upscale output format** to **Lossless FFV1 (RGB)** or **Editing Master MP4** when the result will go through more editing or another workflow. - **Before running again.** Keep the footage you want to process visible on Video and mute competing takes.
